literal: In midsummer one teaches setting up camp, arrayed like the marshaled columns, then conducts the seedling hunt, following the methods of the great hunt.
idiomatic: In midsummer troops are taught to set camp, arrayed as in marshaling the columns, then the seedling hunt is held by the same methods as the great hunt.

literal: The captured game is offered in the yue sacrifice.
idiomatic: The captured game is offered in the yue sacrifice.

literal: In mid-autumn one teaches ordering the troops, arrayed like the marshaled columns, then conducts the extermination hunt, following the methods of the great hunt.
idiomatic: In mid-autumn troops are taught to order the ranks, arrayed as in marshaling the columns, then the extermination hunt is held by the same methods as the great hunt.

literal: The captured game is presented in sacrifice to the directional altar.
idiomatic: The captured game is presented in sacrifice at the directional altar.

literal: In mid-winter one teaches the great review, then conducts the winter hunt.
idiomatic: In mid-winter the great review is taught, then the winter hunt is held.

literal: The captured game is offered in the winter sacrifice.
idiomatic: The captured game is offered in the winter sacrifice.

literal: The great hunt means to gather and take those not bearing young.
idiomatic: The great hunt gathers game but takes only those not bearing young.

literal: The seedling hunt means merely to remove pests for the seedlings.
idiomatic: The seedling hunt is only for clearing pests from the seedlings.

literal: The extermination hunt means killing.
idiomatic: The extermination hunt means killing.

literal: It follows the autumn qi, by which much is killed.
idiomatic: It follows the autumn qi, the season when much is killed.

literal: The winter hunt means that when winter's creatures are fully grown, one takes what is caught and chooses nothing in particular.
idiomatic: The winter hunt comes when winter's creatures are fully grown: what is caught is taken, with no special selection.

literal: In Han ritual, on the day of Beginning of Autumn, after the suburban sacrifice was finished, martial display was first raised; a victim was beheaded in the suburbs and offered to the imperial tombs—the rite was called the Leopard Slaying.
idiomatic: In Han ritual, on Beginning of Autumn, after the suburban sacrifice was complete, martial display was first raised. A victim was beheaded in the suburbs and offered to the imperial tombs—the rite was called the Leopard Slaying.

literal: In the rite, the imperial carriage rode the war chariot with a white horse and red mane; the emperor personally held the crossbow and shot the victim.
idiomatic: In the rite the emperor rode the war chariot with a white horse and red mane and personally shot the victim with a crossbow.

literal: The Grand Steward ordered the capture cart to convey it to the imperial tombs.
idiomatic: The Grand Steward ordered the capture cart to carry it to the imperial tombs.

literal: Thereupon the imperial carriage returned to the palace, and envoys were sent to bestow bundles of silk on military officers; the arts of Sun and Wu and the formations of battle were practiced—this became the regular custom.
idiomatic: The emperor then returned to the palace and sent envoys to bestow silk on military officers. The arts of Sun and Wu and the formations of battle were drilled, and this became the regular custom.

literal: In the twenty-first year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian, the relevant offices of Wei memorialized: "In antiquity military instruction was given in all four seasons, always in the gaps between agricultural work.
idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian, Wei's relevant offices memorialized: "In antiquity military instruction was given in all four seasons, always during the gaps in farm work.

literal: Han's Western Capital followed Qin institutions: in three seasons there was no instruction—only in the tenth month was there the capital review.
idiomatic: The Western Capital of Han followed Qin practice: in three seasons there was no instruction—only in the tenth month was the capital review held.

literal: Now arms are not yet laid aside, and officers and people are already practiced—there need be no four-season military instruction.
idiomatic: Now arms are not yet laid aside, and officers and people are already well trained—four-season instruction is unnecessary.

literal: But on Beginning of Autumn choose an auspicious day for the great assembly of chariots and horsemen, called ordering the troops.
idiomatic: But on Beginning of Autumn an auspicious day should be chosen for the great assembly of chariots and horsemen, called ordering the troops.

literal: Above it matches the ritual name; below it continues Han institutions.
idiomatic: Above it matches the ritual name; below it continues Han practice.

literal: " The memorial was approved.
idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

literal: That winter, troops were ordered.
idiomatic: That winter the troops were ordered.

literal: The King of Wei personally beat the gongs and drums to command advance and retreat.
idiomatic: The King of Wei personally beat gongs and drums to command advance and retreat.

literal: In the first year of Yankang, Cao Pi was King of Wei; that year in the sixth month at Beginning of Autumn, troops were ordered in the eastern suburb, with princes and ministers assisting in the rite.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yankang, Cao Pi was King of Wei. That sixth month, at Beginning of Autumn, troops were ordered in the eastern suburb, with princes and ministers assisting in the rite.

literal: The king rode beneath the flowered canopy and personally commanded the cadences of gongs and drums.
idiomatic: The king rode beneath the flowered canopy and personally commanded the cadences of gongs and drums.

literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Taihe under Emperor Ming, troops were ordered in the eastern suburb.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Taihe under Emperor Ming, troops were ordered in the eastern suburb.

literal: In the fourth and ninth years of Taishi, the first year of Xianning, and the fourth and sixth years of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin—all in winter—the emperor personally visited the Xuanwu Viewing Stand and conducted the great review of the assembled armies.
idiomatic: In the fourth and ninth years of Taishi, the first year of Xianning, and the fourth and sixth years of Taikang under Jin Emperor Wu—all in winter—the emperor personally visited the Xuanwu Viewing Stand and conducted the great review of the assembled armies.

literal: Yet he did not personally command advance and retreat.
idiomatic: Yet he did not personally command advance and retreat.

literal: From Emperor Hui onward, the rite was abandoned.
idiomatic: From Emperor Hui onward, the rite was abandoned.

literal: In the fourth year of Daxing under Emperor Yuan, an edict ordered the Left and Right Guards and the various camps to practice drill, making goose-wing arms according to the great review rite.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daxing under Emperor Yuan, an edict ordered the Left and Right Guards and the various camps to practice drill, making goose-wing arms according to the great review rite.

literal: In the Xianhe era under Emperor Cheng, an edict ordered the inner and outer armies to perform mock battle on the field south of the southern suburb—hence the place was named the Fighting Ground.
idiomatic: In the Xianhe era under Emperor Cheng, an edict ordered the inner and outer armies to perform mock battle on the field south of the southern suburb—hence the place was named the Fighting Ground.

literal: Afterward the frontier commanders Huan, Yu, and other regional lords often conducted reviews, yet at court nothing was done.
idiomatic: Afterward frontier commanders such as Huan and Yu often held reviews, yet the court itself did nothing.

literal: While the Founding Emperor was on the throne, he practiced drill of the assembled armies according to precedent, using both Han and Wei rites together.
idiomatic: While Emperor Wen was on the throne, he drilled the assembled armies according to precedent, combining Han and Wei rites.

literal: Afterward military instruction was given at the Xuanwu Hall according to the season.
idiomatic: Afterward military instruction was given at the Xuanwu Hall according to the season.

literal: In the intercalary second month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, a great hunt was held at the Xuanwu Field; the presiding office, following the edict, submitted the schedule and arrangements, fixed the day for the military hunt, and all officials made ready.
idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia a great hunt was held at the Xuanwu Field. The presiding office, following the edict, submitted the schedule, fixed the day for the military hunt, and all officials made ready.

literal: A traveling palace hall with a military tent for informal seating was set up on the southern hill of the headquarters mountain.
idiomatic: A traveling palace hall with a military tent for informal seating was set up on the southern hill of the headquarters mountain.

literal: Informal seating tents for princes, dukes, and the hundred officials were set up according to the usual rite; four rows of banner gates were set up—north, south, left, and right.
idiomatic: Informal tents for princes, dukes, and officials were set up according to the usual rite, with four rows of banner gates to north, south, left, and right.

literal: Capture banners were erected to mark the capture carts.
idiomatic: Capture banners were erected to mark the capture carts.

literal: One Palace Gentleman served as master of the capture carts.
idiomatic: One Palace Gentleman served as master of the capture carts.

literal: Two stewards collected the game.
idiomatic: Two stewards collected the game.

literal: Twenty-four clerks were assigned to the capture carts.
idiomatic: Twenty-four clerks were assigned to the capture carts.

literal: Twelve capture carts were prepared.
idiomatic: Twelve capture carts were prepared.

literal: Officers of the military hunt wore trousers and short jackets.
idiomatic: Officers of the military hunt wore trousers and short jackets.

literal: Those wearing the martial cap with chin strap did so.
idiomatic: Those wearing the martial cap with chin strap kept it on.

literal: Those removing the cap put on the tassel headband.
idiomatic: Those removing the cap put on the tassel headband.

literal: Those of the second rank and above carried swords at the side and were equipped with spears and command banners; those of the third rank and below wore swords at the belt.
idiomatic: Those of the second rank and above carried swords at the side and were equipped with spears and command banners; those of the third rank and below wore swords at the belt.

literal: All rode on horseback.
idiomatic: All rode on horseback.

literal: The generals' units hunted one day in advance, sending detachments to deploy the encirclement.
idiomatic: The generals' units hunted one day in advance, sending detachments to deploy the encirclement.

literal: One General Who Leads the Army supervised the right wing;
idiomatic: One General Who Leads the Army supervised the right wing;

literal: One Protector General supervised the left wing;
idiomatic: one Protector General supervised the left wing;

literal: One Grand Marshal stood at the center, correcting all armies, all receiving his command.
idiomatic: and one Grand Marshal stood at the center, directing all armies, all under his command.

literal: The Palace Gentleman led the capture-cart units behind the Marshal.
idiomatic: The Palace Gentleman led the capture-cart units behind the Marshal.

literal: The Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Director of Judgments, Director of the Five Armies, Left and Right Vice Directors, the various bureau gentlemen of Judgments, chief clerks, clerks of the various bureaus of Judgments, clerks of the Orchid Terrace Secretariat and Imperial Censorate, and clerks of the various bureaus supervised and corrected violations at the military hunt.
idiomatic: The Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Director of Judgments, Director of the Five Armies, Left and Right Vice Directors, bureau gentlemen, chief clerks, and clerks of the Judgments, Secretariat, and Censorate offices supervised and corrected violations at the hunt.

literal: On the day, they assembled at the Xuanwu Field and formed a double encirclement.
idiomatic: On the appointed day they assembled at the Xuanwu Field and formed a double encirclement.

literal: Positions for garrison duty filling the streets were set north of the inner official road and south of the outer official road outside the Cloud Dragon Gate, with west as the place of honor.
idiomatic: Garrison positions filling the streets were set north of the inner official road and south of the outer official road outside the Cloud Dragon Gate, with west as the place of honor.

literal: Positions for attendant officials were set north of the great official steps and south of the lesser official steps inside the Cloud Dragon Gate, with west as the place of honor.
idiomatic: Positions for attendant officials were set north of the great official steps and south of the lesser official steps inside the Cloud Dragon Gate, with west as the place of honor.

literal: Positions for officials placed in advance were set west of the inner official road and east of the outer official road outside the Traveling Halt Gate, with north as the place of honor.
idiomatic: Positions for officials placed in advance were set west of the inner official road and east of the outer official road outside the Traveling Halt Gate, with north as the place of honor.

literal: Return positions for officials placed in advance were set east and west along the road outside the Broad Mo Gate, with south as the place of honor.
idiomatic: Return positions for officials placed in advance were set east and west along the road outside the Broad Mo Gate, with south as the place of honor.

literal: On the day of the military hunt, at dawn the duty Attendant-in-Ordinary announced martial alert.
idiomatic: On the day of the military hunt, at dawn the duty Attendant-in-Ordinary announced the first martial alert.

literal: At one quarter before the water clock's upper mark, it was announced: "Strike one drum.
idiomatic: One quarter before the water clock's upper mark came the announcement: "Strike one drum.

literal: " This was the first alert.
idiomatic: This was the first alert.

literal: At two quarters before the upper mark, it was announced: "Strike two drums.
idiomatic: Two quarters before the upper mark came: "Strike two drums.

literal: " This was the second alert.
idiomatic: This was the second alert.

literal: The Palace Attendant announced the opening of the East Central Flower Cloud Dragon Gate and led out the guard as the small imperial escort.
idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced the opening of the East Central Flower Cloud Dragon Gate and led out the guard as the small imperial escort.

literal: Officials not of the military hunt, wearing vermilion robes, assembled outside the Broad Mo Gate.
idiomatic: Officials not taking part in the hunt, wearing vermilion robes, assembled outside the Broad Mo Gate.

literal: Those who should return to their offices returned.
idiomatic: Those who should return to their offices did so.

literal: The garrison filling the streets and the rear attendant officials took their positions;
idiomatic: The garrison filling the streets and the rear attendant officials took their positions;

literal: The front attendant officials followed the imperial escort;
idiomatic: the front attendant officials followed the imperial escort;

literal: The officials placed in advance went ahead.
idiomatic: and the officials placed in advance went ahead.

literal: At three quarters before the upper mark, it was announced: "Strike three drums.
idiomatic: Three quarters before the upper mark came: "Strike three drums.

literal: " This was the third alert.
idiomatic: This was the third alert.

literal: At four quarters before the upper mark, it was announced: "The outer preparations are complete.
idiomatic: Four quarters before the upper mark came: "The outer preparations are complete.

literal: The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary, Regular Palace Attendant, Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary, and military officers with swords and shoes advanced on either side of the upper gate.
idiomatic: The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary, Regular Palace Attendant, Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary, and military officers with swords and shoes advanced on either side of the upper gate.

literal: The duty Vice Attendant carried the imperial seal; the Master of Protocol Clerk carried the tortoise seal of the Secretariat—the seal of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: The duty Vice Attendant carried the imperial seal; the Master of Protocol Clerk carried the tortoise seal of the Secretariat—the seal of the Masters of Writing.

literal: At five quarters before the upper mark, the emperor emerged.
idiomatic: Five quarters before the upper mark, the emperor emerged.

literal: He wore a black kerchief cap and unlined robe and rode in the palanquin.
idiomatic: He wore a black kerchief cap and unlined robe and rode in the palanquin.

literal: The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary carried the seal and accompanied him in the carriage, without sword.
idiomatic: The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary carried the seal and rode with him, without sword.

literal: The Palace Attendant supervised and corrected those within the yellow banner.
idiomatic: The Palace Attendant supervised those within the yellow banner.

literal: The alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary and alternate Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary escorted in front.
idiomatic: The alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary and alternate Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary escorted in front.

literal: Again the alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary wore the trust seal and traveling seal, and with the duty Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary followed escorting from behind.
idiomatic: Again the alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary wore the trust seal and traveling seal and, with the duty Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary, followed escorting from behind.

literal: Drums and horns were not sounded; no clamor was permitted; they were led out in order with the usual clearing of the way.
idiomatic: Drums and horns were not sounded; no clamor was permitted; they were led out in order with the usual clearing of the way.

literal: When the imperial carriage emerged, the outriders announced; those on the steps bowed twice.
idiomatic: When the imperial carriage emerged, the outriders announced; those on the steps bowed twice.

literal: The crown prince entered to stand guard.
idiomatic: The crown prince entered to stand guard.

literal: As the imperial carriage was about to arrive, the guard of honor called: "Lead the front attendant officials placed in advance to their positions.
idiomatic: As the imperial carriage was about to arrive, the guard of honor called: "Lead the front attendant officials placed in advance to their positions.

literal: They bowed twice.
idiomatic: They bowed twice.

literal: When the imperial carriage reached the traveling hall and turned the palanquin, the duty Attendant-in-Ordinary knelt and announced: "Descend from the palanquin.
idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached the traveling hall and turned, the duty Attendant-in-Ordinary knelt and announced: "Descend from the palanquin.

literal: The alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary proclaimed the command: "It is permitted.
idiomatic: The alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary proclaimed the command: "It is permitted.

literal: The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary bowed low and rose.
idiomatic: The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary bowed low and rose.

literal: The emperor descended from the palanquin and ascended the imperial seat; attendant ministers ascended the hall.
idiomatic: The emperor descended from the palanquin and ascended the imperial seat; attendant ministers ascended the hall.

literal: The direct guards with halberds drawn from scabbards, tiger guards with plumed-head patterned robes and pheasant-tail feathers, lined the steps in order.
idiomatic: The direct guards with halberds drawn from scabbards, tiger guards in plumed-head patterned robes with pheasant-tail feathers, lined the steps in order.

literal: The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary announced: "Release martial alert.
idiomatic: The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary announced: "Release martial alert.

literal: The officials placed in advance who had escorted the emperor returned to the informal tent offices.
idiomatic: The officials placed in advance who had escorted the emperor returned to the informal tent offices.

literal: If the emperor personally shot game, he changed to military dress; inner and outer attendant officials and the tiger guards all changed dress according to the military hunt rite.
idiomatic: If the emperor personally shot game, he changed to military dress; inner and outer attendants and the tiger guards all changed dress according to the military hunt rite.

literal: Halberds were drawn from scabbards to serve as military guard.
idiomatic: Halberds were drawn from scabbards to serve as military guard.

literal: Inner officials within the yellow banner followed into the encirclement.
idiomatic: Inner officials within the yellow banner followed into the encirclement.

literal: Units were deployed in array; the wing encirclement was spread wide; flags and drums faced one another; they advanced with gags in the mouth.
idiomatic: Units were deployed in array; the wing encirclement was spread wide; flags and drums faced one another; they advanced with gags in their mouths.

literal: When the wings closed the encirclement, the wing command clerks galloped and shouted the legal command: "In spring birds and beasts with young are gathered but not shot;
idiomatic: When the wings closed the encirclement, the wing command clerks galloped and shouted the legal command: "In spring, birds and beasts with young are gathered but not shot;

literal: The flesh of birds and beasts not placed on the sacrificial stand—do not shoot;
idiomatic: the flesh of birds and beasts not destined for the sacrificial stand—do not shoot;

literal: Hide, teeth, bone, horn, feather, and down not placed in vessels—do not shoot.
idiomatic: hide, teeth, bone, horn, feather, and down not destined for use—do not shoot.

literal: " The wings closed.
idiomatic: The wings closed.
